Subject: High 5xx/429 and long-tail latency — Private deployment (VPC peer)

Hi Vivek,

We started seeing a sustained elevation in 5xx and 429 responses from Redwood for our private deployment around 02:15 UTC (04/15). The errors are concentrated on the tokenization/response stage and correlate with long tail latencies (p95 -> 12s+). This is impacting settlement jobs — ~4% of transactions are failing and retry traffic is spiking on our side.

Attached: error_sample.log (snippets of 5xx responses), packet_capture.pcap (tcp, 15s window).

Top observed symptoms: 
- 5xx and 429 bursts that start suddenly and then decay over ~30–90 minutes
- Frequent client timeouts followed by retries which amplify load
- Errors appear only for requests routed to our dedicated VPC peer (private deployment) — hosted API unaffected

Can you confirm if there were any planned changes? We need an incident bridge and an immediate mitigation plan. Our compliance team is watching.

Thanks,
Aaron Lewis
Ops Lead, BlueHarbor Finance

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-15T08:22:00-04:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial packet captures + quick triage notes

Forwarding packet capture we pulled from the customer. Quick notes from initial triage: 
- Observed many TCP connections stalling in CLOSE_WAIT and a high rate of TCP retransmits on the path between customer's NAT and our private ingress.
- NAT ephemeral port exhaustion is plausible — we see many short-lived connections with identical source IPs and increasing SYN retries.
- On our side, the Private peering path shows spike in connection queueing at the edge proxy (queue depth up 4-6x usual for the interval).

Immediate mitigations to try now (low-risk):
- Increase NAT ephemeral port pool on the customer's NAT (ask BlueHarbor ops) and on our egress when using shared NAT for fallback.
- Temporarily enable a conservative rate-limiter at the private ingress for this tenant to drop retry amplification (set to 150 rps per client ip).
- Add a short connection timeout and connection re-use tuning (keepalive) on the runtime side to avoid accumulation.

If NAT exhaustion is confirmed, we'll coordinate with the customer for a longer-term fix (split NAT pool, SNAT per subnet, or deploy dedicated NAT gateway).

Laura
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Aaron / Samantha — quick update from the bridge: 
- Root-cause candidate: NAT ephemeral port exhaustion on the customer's NAT combined with connection queueing at the private ingress. This caused timeouts, triggering retry loops and amplifying load.
- Immediate mitigations performed: increased connection keepalive, applied per-client soft rate limit at the private ingress, and asked your ops to expand the NAT port range as a quick fix.
- Initial effect: error rate fell ~60% and tail latency p95 dropped from ~12s to ~3.8s for affected routes.

Next steps (owned):
- BlueHarbor ops: confirm NAT port expansion and keep traffic steady for 30 minutes so we can validate stability (owner: Aaron).
- Redwood SRE: follow-up action to provision a dedicated NAT gateway for BlueHarbor on the peered VPC (owner: Laura).
- Redwood CS: prepare potential SLA/credit guidance if we see any persistent customer impact (owner: Marissa).

We will keep you updated every 30 minutes while we validate.

— Vivek

Subject: Incident wrap and next steps (INC-9276)

Team — final post-incident summary for INC-9276. 

What happened: customer VPC peer experienced ephemeral port exhaustion during a traffic burst; combined with ingress queueing at our private edge, this produced a cascade of timeouts and retry amplification that manifested as elevated 5xx/429 for BlueHarbor.

Immediate fixes applied: 
- Expanded customer NAT ephemeral port range (customer action).
- Temporary per-client soft rate limiter on private ingress (Redwood config).
- Keepalive/reuse tuning applied to runtime to reduce connection churn.

Resolution: after NAT expansion + ingress limiter p95 latency returned to baseline and 5xx rate reduced to <0.1%. BlueHarbor confirmed critical job success improved from 96% -> 99.7% over 24h.

Follow-ups (owners & ETA):
- Laura (SRE): provision dedicated NAT gateway for BlueHarbor and validate peering MTU + route MTU settings (ETA 72h).
- Marissa (CS): finalize SLA/credit guidance and run exec call if customer requests (ETA 24h).
- Vivek (Sales): coordinate account communications and renewal risk evaluation (ongoing).

Attachments: redwood_support_brief.pdf (post-incident mitigation plan).

Monica Patel
Support Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
